deities: Sri Guru Granth Sahib (the Sikh scripture enshrined as the eternal Guru - Sikh worship is non-idolatrous)
festivals: Gurpurabs (birth anniversaries of the Sikh Gurus)

history.summary: THIS IS A SIKH GURDWARA, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Gurdwara Singh Sabha in Sector 19-D, Chandigarh, is a modern community gurdwara built by local Sikhs in the 1980s; per SikhiWiki it has no historical background. It includes a sarai (guesthouse) with 32 individual rooms (double bed, cupboard, shared toilets), with stays up to 3 days. CSV town 'Chandigarh' is correct, but CSV state 'Punjab' is wrong - Chandigarh is a Union Territory.

name: Gurdwara Singh Sabha
town_description: Chandigarh is a planned city and Union Territory serving as the joint capital of Punjab and Haryana, designed by Le Corbusier and known as 'The City Beautiful'. Sector 19 is a residential sector in the city; its Gurdwara Singh Sabha is a modern community place of worship with an attached sarai for travellers.

travel.road: In Sector 19-D, Chandigarh; well connected by city buses, autos and taxis.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Baisakhi and Gurpurabs for major gatherings.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily diwan (congregational prayers) morning and evening; langar served daily. Exact hours not published (verify). Free entry; cover head and remove shoes before entry.
